Week 7 is here and it is time to learn about regularization. Regularization methods were first invented to handle problems in the applied sciences, with first application (that I am aware
of) in the geosciences to estiamte the internal structure of the Earth from sparse measurements. Regularization methods have since spread and become highly developed. They allow for 
models of arbitrary complexity to be used in situations where they would normally overfit. Regularization methods achieve this by penalizing models for assigning values to coefficients
different than 0, causing "shrinkage" of coefficients. This increases bias, but reduces variance and thus helps with overfitting. We will learn about the two most important regularization 
methods, _Ridge_ regression (or an $L_2$ penalty) and the _Lasso_ (or an $L_1$ penalty). 

You can read more about the plan for the week and the reading/resources in [Module 7](../modules/module7.qmd).
